clue.text: Good fellow with measure that provides material for the house

definitions.text: that provides material for the house
definitions.note: a clause describing a place, standing in for the noun

blocks.note: calling someone a brick is old British praise for a reliable, generous person
a yard is an imperial measure of length, three feet

explanation.surface: A decent chap with a tape measure who supplies the materials for building a house.
explanation.walkthrough: A brick is the good fellow, and bricks are also what the yard turns out, so the wordplay and definition share a theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickyard is the works where bricks are made, the raw stuff walls of a home are built from.

clue.text: Fleeting beauty of opera

blocks.note: surface reading: a short-lived lovely thing, a passing glory
setter's reading: a short-lived winged insect that also names the heroine of Puccini's Madama opera

explanation.surface: A lament for the brief loveliness of an operatic heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly lends its title; the insect lives only briefly, hence fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged insect lives briefly and is admired for its colours, and Puccini named a famous opera after one.

clue.text: Like Gray's tower, I contended

blocks.note: taken as written
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: A poet's tower, and someone claiming to have competed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard mentions 'yonder ivy-mantled tower'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tower in Gray's Elegy is ivy-mantled, which is to say overgrown and covered with climbing ivy.

clue.text: Measure of the power in the House

definitions.text: Measure of the power in the House

blocks.note: surface reading: political influence in the House of Commons

blocks.clueFragment: Measure of the power in the House
blocks.note: setter's reading: a unit of electrical power as metered in a home, a thousand of the units named after James Watt

explanation.surface: Gauging how much political clout someone holds in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes it the House of Commons, but the power is electricity in an ordinary house.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic electricity is metered and billed in units of a thousand watts, so this unit measures household power.

clue.text: Pompadour's long-range weather forecast

blocks.note: surface reading: a meteorological prediction for weeks ahead
setter's reading: Madame de Pompadour's reputed remark 'après nous le déluge', a prophecy of the flood after her time

explanation.surface: A royal mistress offering a forecast of the weather to come.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame de Pompadour, mistress of Louis XV, is credited with 'après nous le déluge': after us, the flood.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous French saying predicts a great flood after her day, a deluge being an overwhelming downpour.

clue.text: Band helping resist underground movement

definitions.note: a description of a thing, standing in for the noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat strip of leather or fabric
second meaning: the hanging loop a standing passenger grips on a lurching Tube train

explanation.surface: A group aiding the Resistance, the underground movement of wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: The underground movement looks like the wartime Resistance; it is the jolting of a London Underground carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather loop is a strip of material, and standing commuters grip it to steady themselves against the train's motion.

clue.text: Sailor implies that virtue is a good thing?

blocks.clueFragment: Sailor implies that virtue is a good thing
blocks.note: surface reading: a seaman offering a moral opinion

blocks.clueFragment: implies that virtue is a good thing
blocks.note: setter's reading: the name read as two words states that wrongdoing is wicked, so its opposite must be good

explanation.surface: An old salt hinting that virtue is a worthy thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the sailor's name into two words and it reads as a moral verdict on wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabian Nights hero made seven voyages, so he is the most famous seafarer of legend.

clue.text: Thinking a nose is broken in boxing arena

indicators.note: something broken has its parts knocked out of their order
placing one thing in another means one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: boxers fight in a roped square called a ring
the letters of these words rearranged

explanation.surface: A boxer thinking about the nose broken in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Working something out logically is thinking, the process of drawing conclusions from evidence.

clue.text: The part to play ?

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase standing for a noun: something to be performed

blocks.note: first meaning: a portion or fragment of something
second meaning: a musical composition or a chessman, something performed or moved

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an actor's role; the two meanings are a portion and a composition for performing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a portion of a whole, and also a musical work or a chessman someone performs or moves.

clue.text: Musical TTT

blocks.note: surface reading: a stage show or song with a cryptic three-letter title
setter's reading: one letter written three times over, a group of three

explanation.surface: The title of a stage show, written as three letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Three identical Ts form a set of three, and in music a group of three notes played in the time of two has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: In notation, three notes squeezed into the time of two form a group named for the number three.

clue.text: Facial mark, what it shows of one's pedigree

blocks.note: a line is a wrinkle on the face
wrinkles show how old a person is

explanation.surface: A wrinkle betraying the years, as if reading ancestry in a face.
explanation.walkthrough: The second piece follows from the first: what a wrinkle shows is how old you are.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a person's ancestry, the line of descent from forebears.

clue.text: Invest the same again in different quarters

indicators.note: one thing set in others is placed inside them

blocks.note: three different compass points, east, north and west
short for ditto, used in lists to mean the same as above

explanation.surface: An investor putting the same sum again into different districts.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters are the points of the compass, and DO is the abbreviation for ditto.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest someone with a quality or funds is to endow them, providing a gift or income.

clue.text: Terribly grim, a part of this confounded yarn ?

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters come out of order

blocks.note: the letters of these words rearranged
an actor's part is a role

explanation.surface: A grim role in a bewildering tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a long, rambling, muddled story, a confusing account that wanders on.

clue.text: Shape of endocarp when split

blocks.note: surface reading: the hard inner layer of a fruit, as in a stone
setter's reading: split into end o' carp, the rear part of a freshwater swimmer

explanation.surface: A botanist describing the form of a fruit stone that has cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: Endocarp is a real botanical term, which is the trap; split it and you get the end of a carp.
explanation.definitionFit: A forked shape like a swimmer's rear fin is named after that fin, as in a skidding car's swerve.

clue.text: Top limit, and reprimand, for brilliant climber

blocks.note: the sky's the limit, meaning no ceiling at all
to get a rocket is British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A rising star given a ceiling and a ticking-off.
explanation.walkthrough: A rocket is British slang for a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: A firework shoots upwards and bursts into dazzling light, so it is a brightly glowing thing that rises.

clue.text: Equal, we hear, to providing seaside attraction

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: a peer is an equal, as in tried by one's peers

explanation.surface: Someone said to be equal to running a seaside amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: British resorts have long wooden walkways out over the sea, with arcades and shows, as holiday amusements.

clue.text: Reserve provision for skaters in replanned centre

indicators.note: a site replanned is laid out afresh, so its letters take a new order
one item put in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
a rink provides skaters with a frozen surface

explanation.surface: A rink for skaters set aside in a redesigned town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve in a person means holding back, keeping quiet about feelings, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Food and water source, a parting wish

blocks.note: fare is food, as in simple country fare
a well is a shaft sunk to draw water

explanation.surface: Supplies of food and water given as a traveller departs.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old goodbye, literally hoping the person leaving will get on well.

clue.text: They are keen to advance up to a point

definitions.text: They are keen to advance up to a point

blocks.clueFragment: keen to advance up to a point
blocks.note: surface reading: ambitious people pushing on, but only so far
setter's reading: literally going up to a summit, a mountain peak

explanation.surface: Ambitious types whose eagerness to get on has its limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Up to a point sounds like a hedge on how keen they are; it is the peak they ascend.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountaineers ascend to summits, and social strivers are eager to rise, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Toy is doubly non-U, you see

indicators.note: non-U literally means without U, so that letter is dropped
doubly means the piece is written out twice in a row

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A toy dismissed as twice over lower-class, you see.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old British label for language the upper classes thought common; here it means remove the U.
explanation.definitionFit: The spinning disc on a string climbs and drops as a child flicks the wrist, a classic plaything.

clue.text: Illumination for actors

blocks.note: surface reading: stage lighting rigged for a cast
setter's reading: also a Patrick Hamilton play, a title for actors to perform

explanation.surface: Lighting set up on stage for the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Victorian theatres were lit by burning coal gas, and the same word is the title of Patrick Hamilton's 1938 thriller.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamps burning coal gas lit Victorian streets and stages, and the word also names a famous stage thriller.

clue.text: Refusal to face about two points

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: dial is slang for a face
east and north, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone refusing to confront a couple of issues.
explanation.walkthrough: Dial is old slang for face; points are compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to a request, or declining to admit something, is a refusal of it.

clue.text: Mark of the golden heart

blocks.note: surface reading: a sign of a kind, generous nature
setter's reading: what an archer aims at, whose centre ring is gold

explanation.surface: A sign that someone has a heart of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: In archery the centre of the board is coloured gold and called the gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The board an archer aims at, with its gold bullseye, is the mark they shoot for.

clue.text: Wood walk ?

blocks.note: surface reading: a stroll through a forest
setter's reading: Sir Henry Wood, conductor who founded the London concerts named after a strolling walk

explanation.surface: A stroll through the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood founded the Proms, London's summer concerts, short for this word because the audience originally stood and strolled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a leisurely stroll or seafront walkway, and gave its name to the concerts Henry Wood conducted.

clue.text: In the field he may take cover

definitions.text: In the field he may take cover

blocks.clueFragment: In the field he may take cover
blocks.note: surface reading: a soldier on the battlefield ducking for shelter
setter's reading: a cricket fielder whose position sits next to the one called cover, and may stand in for it

explanation.surface: A soldier in the field diving for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, point and cover are neighbouring fielding positions on the off side; cover point lies between them.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the word names a fielding position square of the batsman, beside the cover position.

clue.text: Sort of lantern that can be black and white

definitions.text: Sort of lantern that can be black and white

blocks.clueFragment: lantern that can be black and white
blocks.note: surface reading: a projector showing monochrome pictures
setter's reading: sorcery comes as the black kind and the white kind

explanation.surface: An old slide projector throwing monochrome images.
explanation.walkthrough: A magic lantern was an early slide projector; black and white are the evil and benign kinds of sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: The early projector was called a magic lantern, and sorcery is divided into black and white varieties.

clue.text: Beg us to show taste

indicators.note: the words show, or display, a run of letters sitting within them

blocks.note: a run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: Pleading with someone to display some good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Italian for relish or flavour, so it can mean taste as well as zest.

clue.text: Suspicion of fashionable monarch accepting money

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: in means in fashion
a king is a monarch
L stands for the pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Suspicion that a trendy king is taking bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from the Latin libra.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint suspicion or vague idea is a hint of knowledge, which is what this word describes.

clue.text: Potential English sermon writer

indicators.note: something potential could become something else, so these letters may form a new word

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English sermon with the makings of a writer in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Waldo Emerson, the American essayist, was himself a Unitarian minister, so the sermon fits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet, an author of transcendentalist works.

clue.text: Complete some, say

definitions.note: stands for the homophone sum, a noun

indicators.note: say asks for the word as spoken aloud rather than as spelt

blocks.note: first meaning: whole, absolute
second meaning: a word spoken the same as this one, an amount added up

explanation.walkthrough: Some sounds like sum, and an amount added up is the answer as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means utter or entire; as a noun it is the figure reached by adding up.

clue.text: Far-seeing resolution is its purpose

blocks.note: surface reading: a visionary decision or determination
setter's reading: an optical instrument's job is resolving detail at great distance

explanation.surface: A visionary resolve taken as a mission statement.
explanation.walkthrough: Resolution looks like determination; in optics it is the power to separate fine detail.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical instrument for viewing distant objects is judged by how finely it can separate detail.
